The improvement is partly achieved by moving substantial production load into already busy earlier days. Tuesday now has Gym & Cardio Session 10:00-11:30, Thumbnail & Video Export 12:30-16:30, added Video Recording Block 16:30-19:00, and Evening Live Stream 20:00-23:30. Wednesday has Gym Workout 10:00-11:30, Scriptwriting 12:30-16:30, added Video Recording Block 16:30-19:00, Dinner with Creator Friends 19:30-21:30, and Evening Live Stream 22:00-00:30. These are conflict-free but dense sequences with limited visible margin for food, setup, decompression, or quality recovery.

Thursday remains demanding despite the new buffer: Gym Workout 10:00-11:30 is followed by Final Editing & Publishing 12:30-16:30, then a recovery buffer 16:30-19:00, then the 6-hour stream 19:00-01:00. The buffer helps, but the rationale does not explain whether a 4-hour final publishing block immediately before the marathon is compatible with the intended quality and energy level for the launch stream.

The proposal labels the 16:30-19:00 Thursday block as recovery, but it immediately follows 4 hours of final editing/publishing and directly precedes a 6-hour live stream. It may be useful recovery, but the calendar alone does not show whether it includes dinner, stream setup, technical checks, hygiene, or actual rest.

The alternatives considered are relevant to protected sleep, gym, and avoiding late Friday work, but they do not substantially address whether the added Tuesday and Wednesday recording blocks are the most sustainable distribution within the visible week, or whether the Thursday pre-marathon editing load should be reduced, buffered differently, or better substantiated.

The rationale acknowledges hidden dependencies for splitting recording and moving editing, but the final schedule depends heavily on those assumptions being true. If recording has Thursday-specific content, resource availability, or setup continuity needs, the new distribution could undermine the visible production goal.
prior_critic_reviews.feedback: This is a stronger plan than the prior version because it no longer leaves a 5-hour recording block directly before the Thursday marathon and it creates explicit recovery time after the marathon. However, the revised calendar still raises a material human-manageability concern: the proposal redistributes the load rather than clearly reducing it, producing dense production-and-stream sequences on Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday. The Proposer should reconsider or better substantiate whether the added recording blocks after existing 4-hour production blocks, plus the moved Thursday final editing block before the 6-hour launch stream, are realistically sustainable for the user. The same operations might be acceptable with fuller context, but the current rationale does not yet show that the earlier-week compression and pre-marathon cognitive load are a good trade-off. Request satisfaction cannot be independently verified because the original request and full user context are not provided.
